Here’s the complete 12-week program summary for your 29-year-old recreational climber with right subacromial impingement. Constraints: pain-free range only; no overhead loading. Full gym available. Program includes upper-body strength (primary), cardio 2x/week, hangboard/climbing prep (later phases), mobility, nutrition, and a Saturday finisher. Structure is week-by-week with phased progression, deloads, and a Week-12 peak for a climbing trip.

Global guardrails
- Absolutely pain-free; stop any exercise that causes shoulder pain or next-day ache. Prioritize neutral/semisupinated grips, elbows 30–45° from torso on presses, and scapulae “long and down.” Avoid overhead presses/pulls, vertical hangs, high abduction, kips, dynamic reaches, or gastons.
- Progression order: range of motion (pain-free) → load → sets/reps. RPE 6–7 early, up to 7–8 by mid/late phases if symptom-free.
- Weekly cadence (ideal): 3 UB sessions (A/B/C), 2 cardio, 1–2 hangboard/climbing-prep (Phases 2–3), daily brief mobility, Saturday finisher (optional and scaled).

Warm-up (all sessions, 10–12 min)
- 3–5 min light cardio
- T-spine: open books 6–8/side
- Scap activation: band serratus punches x12; scap depressions x8–10 at incline/support
- Cuff: band/cable ER at 0–30° abd x10/side
- 2–3 progressive warm-up sets for first two lifts

PHASE 1 (Weeks 1–4): Control and tolerance
Goal: Pain-free movement, scapular mechanics, cuff/mid-back endurance, grip tolerance. 2–3 UB sessions/week.

UB-A (horizontal push + cuff/scap)
- DB floor press (neutral), pain-free ROM
- Chest-supported rear delt fly (thumbs up)
- Landmine press to shoulder height (half-kneel)
- Cable ER at 0–30° abd
- Serratus wall slides (to shoulder height), Prone low Y (100–120°)

UB-B (horizontal pull)
- Chest-supported row (neutral)
- Serratus reach/downward punch (cable)
- 1-arm cable row (low to navel)
- Iso retraction/depression holds (supported)
- Hammer curl, rope pressdown

UB-C (optional light technique)
- Incline push-up (height to pain-free)
- Wrist pronation/supination
- Farmer carry (neutral grip), light-moderate
- Scap pull-up isometrics at bottom (depression only)

Loading guide Weeks 1–3: 3–4 sets x 8–12 reps main work at RPE 6–7; controlled tempo (e.g., 3-1-1/3-1-2). Progress small ROM/load each week if pain-free. Week 4 deload: −30–40% volume, same/light load, technique focus.

PHASE 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength and unilateral control
Goal: Increase horizontal press/pull strength; refine scap/cuff; introduce isometric mid-range work. Prefer 3 UB sessions/week.

UB-A (press emphasis)
- DB bench (neutral) 4x6–8 (progress to 5x5 by W7)
- Rear delt fly (pause)
- Landmine press 4x6 (to shoulder height)
- Cable ER at 45° abd
- Serratus wall slides; Pallof press

UB-B (pull emphasis)
- 1-arm chest-supported row 4x8/side
- Face pull to chest/neck height (light, elbows low)
- Seated cable row 4x8–10 (neutral)
- Prone T/Y holds (below overhead)
- Reverse or hammer curls; triceps cable ext (neutral)

UB-C (unilateral + grip)
- Incline push-up (lower incline across phase; flat only if fully pain-free)
- Landmine press isometrics (safe angle)
- Carries: farmer or bottoms-up (light)
- Scap depressions

Week 8 deload: −40% sets, RPE 6–7, ROM quality and scap/cuff drills.

PHASE 3 (Weeks 9–12): Intensification, endurance, peak
Goal: Solidify strength, build climbing-specific finger/forearm endurance and aerobic power, and taper for a Week-12 trip (no overhead loading).

UB-A (press emphasis; keep crisp)
- DB bench: 5x5 (W9), 4x4–5 (W10 deload), 4x3–4 (W11), W12 1–2 top sets 3–4 at RPE ~7
- Landmine press: 4x6 → 3–4x4–5; stop at shoulder height
- Rear delts + cuff: 2–3 light sets

UB-B (heavy pull emphasis)
- Chest-supported row: 5x5 (W9), 4x4–5 (W10 deload), 5x4 (W11), W12 3x3–4 at RPE 7
- 1-arm cable row with 2s peak holds: 3x6–10/side
- Face pulls light; T/Y holds light

UB-C (keep or drop depending on fatigue)
- Alternating DB floor press, unilateral rows, carries, core; stop 2 reps shy of failure

CARDIO 2x/week (all phases; shoulder-safe modalities: bike, incline treadmill/hike, stair mill, sled pushes, brisk walk)
- Phase 1: Build to 40–45 min Z2
- Phase 2: Extend to 50–60 min Z2 + introduce tempo (e.g., 4x4 min RPE 6–7)
- Phase 3: One long Z2 70–90 min hike + one aerobic-power session (e.g., bike 6x2–3 min RPE 7–8). Week 12: 45–60 min easy Z2 only

HANGBOARD + CLIMBING-SPECIFIC PREP (Phase 2–3; 1–2x/week)
Rules: Pain-free shoulder; elbows 10–30° flexed; scapulae depressed; supported hangs with assistance; open-hand/half-crimp; no overhead dead-hangs/lock-offs.

Phase 2 (W5–8)
- Supported holds on jugs/20–25 mm: 6–12s holds, 4–6 sets, 30–70% BW offload
- Add gentle recruitment pulls (assisted) and 18–20 mm only if symptom-free
- Week 8 deload: reduce to easy assisted jugs/20–25 mm

Phase 3 (W9–12) with Peak
- W9: Repeaters 2–3 sets on 20–22 mm (6 x 7s on/3s off), plus foot-on board circuits 3 x 3 min
- W10: Key session—repeaters on 18–20 mm (3 x 6) if pain-free; ARC 2 x 8–10 min low-angle traversing below shoulder height
- W11: Peak finger load—repeaters 4 x 6 on 18–20 mm or density 5 x 20s on 20–22 mm; ARC 12–15 min continuous easy traverse
- W12 Taper: Recruitment touches only (3 rounds: 3 x 3s, heavy assistance) + short easy traverse 10–12 min; avoid fatigue

SATURDAY FINISHER (25–35 min, fun, full-body; rotate options; no overhead)
- Phase 1 picks: EMOM 20 (rows, landmine to shoulder height or incline push-ups, goblet squats, easy bike) or 4-station circuit x4 (incline push-up, sled/carry, rear delts, reverse lunge)
- Phase 2 picks: AMRAP 25 (farmer carry, 1-arm landmine press, 1-arm cable row, DB RDL, bike) or 12-min ladder (DB floor press + goblet squat) + 6-min finisher (rows/walk)
- Phase 3 picks: 20–24 min blocks (sled + incline push-ups; rows + bike; landmine + farmer hold + brisk walk) or EMOM 24 (row, DB floor press, trap-bar/DB RDL, carry)
- Week 12: keep light and short (10–20 min easy work; no finger fatigue)

MOBILITY (6–15 min most days; pain-free only)
Prep (pre-session, 6–10 min)
- 90/90 breathing (3–4 breaths x 3)
- Open books 6–8/side
- Band serratus punches 2x10; wall slide to shoulder height 2x8–10
- Scap depressions 2x8
- Band/cable ER at 0–30° abd 2x10

Recovery (post/evening, 8–12 min)
- Child’s pose side reach 2x20–30s/side
- Low-angle pec doorway stretch 2x20–30s/side
- Sleeper stretch gentle 2x20s/side (swap to cross-body if provocative) + light band ER 1x12
- Prone low Y 2x10
- Forearm care: wrist flex/ext glides 8–10 reps; extensor band opens 1–2x20

Lower-body mobility (2–3x/week, 6–8 min)
- Ankle dorsiflexion rocks 2x10/side; 90/90 hip switches 2x6–8; adductor rock-backs 2x10; half-kneel hip flexor stretch 2x20–30s/side

NUTRITION (recomposition focus, supports recovery)
- Calories: Train days ~14–15 kcal/lb (30–33 kcal/kg); Rest days ~12–13 kcal/lb (26–29 kcal/kg). Adjust to lose ~0.25–0.5% BW/week; go to maintenance in Week 12.
- Protein: 0.8–1.0 g/lb (1.8–2.2 g/kg) in 3–5 feedings of 25–40 g.
- Carbs: 1.5–2.0 g/lb (3.3–4.4 g/kg) train days; 1.0–1.5 g/lb (2.2–3.3 g/kg) rest days; time most pre/post training.
- Fat: 0.3–0.4 g/lb (0.7–0.9 g/kg).
- Micronutrients: oily fish 2x/week or 1–2 g EPA/DHA; vitamin D3 1,000–2,000 IU if low sun; magnesium 200–400 mg if sleep/cramps; optional collagen 10–15 g + ~50 mg vitamin C 30–60 min pre-training.
- Peri-workout: 25–40 g protein + 60–90 g carbs 60–120 min pre; 25–40 g protein + 40–80 g carbs post. Long cardio/hangs >60–90 min: 20–40 g carbs/hr + electrolytes.
- Week 12: raise to maintenance (+200–300 kcal/day), carbs higher; day before trip 5–7 g/kg carbs.

CARDIO placement
- Place the long Z2 the day after UB-A or UB-B; place the aerobic-power session 48 h away from the longest hangboard/ARC. Avoid back-to-back high-grip days.

PROGRESSION AND DELoadS
- W4 and W8: deload volume 30–40% (technique/ROM focus).
- W9–11: intensify strength (lower reps, RPE 7–8), hangboard repeaters progress (if pain-free), and specific endurance (ARC).
- W12: taper volume 40–60%, keep light intensity touches; arrive fresh.

READINESS/RED FLAGS
- Green: zero shoulder pain during/after, improved ROM, lower HR at same Z2 pace, higher quality repeaters/rows/presses.
- Red: shoulder pinch or night pain; finger A2 tenderness; nerve symptoms. Respond by reducing volume 30–50%, increasing assistance/edge size, swapping to more supported variants, and consulting physio as needed.

Example weekly layout (Phase 3 intensification)
- Mon: UB-A + short recruitment hangboard
- Tue: Long Z2 hike
- Wed: UB-B
- Thu: Hangboard (repeaters) + foot-on or ARC
- Fri: Rest or mobility walk
- Sat: Finisher (shorter if forearms cooked)
- Sun: Aerobic power bike (or swap with Tue if preferred)

- If any exercise provokes symptoms:
  - Reduce ROM or switch to more supported variant (e.g., DB press → floor press; row → chest-supported; push-up → higher incline).
  - Lower abduction angle and use neutral grip.
  - Decrease tempo demands if they cause fatigue-related form breakdown; keep controlled eccentrics.

Return-to-overhead planning (post-Week 12, with physio clearance)
- Begin with unloaded wall slides and dowel scaption within pain-free range, then progress to landmine press to higher arcs, incline presses, and partial-range vertical pulls (assisted). Do not initiate without explicit clearance.

Here’s a simple, sustainable 12-week body-recomposition nutrition plan to pair with the training block. Emphasis: maintain or slightly increase lean mass, reduce fat mass gradually, support shoulder recovery, and fuel climbing/strength sessions. It includes targets, food structure, peri-workout strategy, weekly habits, and adjustments.

Core targets (starting point)
- Calories: ~14–15 kcal per lb bodyweight (30–33 kcal/kg) on training days; ~12–13 kcal/lb (26–29 kcal/kg) on rest days. Expect ~0.25–0.5% bodyweight loss per week. If she’s already quite lean or performance stalls, tighten the deficit less (or move to maintenance).
- Protein: 0.8–1.0 g per lb (1.8–2.2 g/kg) daily. Split into 3–5 feedings of 25–40 g each. Prioritize complete proteins.
- Carbohydrate: 1.5–2.0 g per lb (3.3–4.4 g/kg) on training days; 1.0–1.5 g/lb (2.2–3.3 g/kg) on rest days. Periodize higher carbs around training.
- Fat: 0.3–0.4 g per lb (0.7–0.9 g/kg), adjust to meet calories after setting protein and carbs. Do not dip below 0.3 g/lb for hormonal health.
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day from plants.
- Hydration: 30–40 mL/kg/day; add 500–750 mL per hour of training. Include electrolytes if she sweats heavily.

Peri-workout (for upper-body strength and light climbing)
- 60–120 min pre: balanced meal with 25–40 g protein + 60–90 g low-to-moderate GI carbs; minimal fiber/fat if she gets GI upset.
- 0–30 min post: 25–40 g fast/normal protein + 40–80 g carbs. If appetite is low, a shake plus fruit/cereal or chocolate milk + banana works well.
- Optional during long sessions (>90 min): 20–40 g carbs/hour (sports drink, chews).

Protein choices and distribution
- Animal: eggs/egg whites, Greek skyr/yogurt, cottage cheese, chicken/turkey, lean beef, pork tenderloin, fish (especially oily fish 2x/week for omega-3s), whey/iso.
- Plant: tofu/tempeh, edamame, seitan, lentils, beans, pea/soy protein blends. Combine sources for complete amino acid profile.
- Daily spread example (for a 60–70 kg woman): 4 protein feedings at ~30–35 g each + a 20–30 g snack.

Carb quality and timing
- Emphasize: potatoes, rice, oats, pasta, whole grains, fruit, low-fat dairy, legumes (as tolerated), and easy carbs around training (rice cakes, cereal, bananas).
- Keep most carbs pre/post training; dial carbs down at late-night meals if sleep is affected.

Fats and micronutrients (recovery/shoulder health)
- Include fatty fish or 1–2 g/day combined EPA/DHA if fish intake is low.
- Use olive oil, avocado, nuts/seeds (chia/flax for ALA), and egg yolks.
- Calcium + vitamin D: 2–3 dairy servings/day or supplement D3 (1,000–2,000 IU/day) if deficient or low sun exposure.
- Magnesium: 200–400 mg at night if sleep/cramps are issues.
- Collagen/gelatin + vitamin C (optional for tendons): 10–15 g collagen or 15 g gelatin 30–60 min before training with ~50 mg vitamin C (e.g., half orange/kiwi). Not mandatory, but may support connective tissue.

Sample day templates
- Training day (example ~1,900–2,200 kcal for 60–70 kg):
  - Breakfast: Greek yogurt (250 g) + oats (50–60 g) + berries + honey; coffee; water.
  - Pre-lift snack (60–90 min pre): Rice cakes (3–4) with turkey slices or whey shake + banana.
  - Post-lift: Whey shake + cereal with milk or white rice + fruit.
  - Lunch: Chicken breast (120–150 g) + rice (120–150 g dry cooked equivalent ~ 60–75 g dry) + mixed veg + olive oil drizzle.
  - Dinner: Salmon (120–150 g) + potatoes (300 g) + salad with avocado.
  - Snack: Cottage cheese (150–200 g) + pineapple; or tofu pudding + granola.
- Rest day (example ~1,600–1,900 kcal):
  - Keep protein constant.
  - Reduce carbs by ~25–30% (swap potatoes/rice portions for extra vegetables).
  - Keep healthy fats moderate; add extra salad/veg volume for satiety.

Weekly structure and habits
- Meal frequency: 3 meals + 1–2 snacks works well.
- Plates: aim for 1–2 palms protein, 1–2 fists veg/salad, 1 cupped hand carbs (2 on training meals), 1 thumb fat (2 on rest meals if carbs are lower).
- Non-starchy veg at 2–3 meals/day.
- Alcohol: max 0–3 drinks per week; avoid near training and bed.
- Caffeine: limit after 2 p.m. if sleep suffers.

Adjustments and tracking
- Track: bodyweight 3–4x/week on waking (average weekly), gym performance, appetite, sleep, and shoulder symptoms.
- If average weight isn’t dropping ~0.25–0.5%/week by Week 3:
  - Remove ~100–150 kcal/day (mostly carbs/fats), or add a 20–30 min easy walk 4–5x/week.
- If strength/performance drops or recovery lags:
  - Bring calories to maintenance for 7–10 days (add 200–300 kcal/day), especially carbohydrates around training.
- If hunger high at night:
  - Move more calories to dinner; emphasize high-fiber veg, potatoes, and protein. Consider casein/cottage cheese pre-bed.

12-week cadence
- Weeks 1–2: Establish baseline calories, protein habit, hydration. Don’t chase scale changes yet.
- Weeks 3–6: Mild deficit on rest days; fuel training days. Collagen + vitamin C pre-lift if using it. Aim for consistent 0.25–0.5% BW loss/week.
- Week 7: Diet deload at maintenance for 5–7 days if training feels heavy or adherence slips; otherwise continue.
- Weeks 8–11: Resume mild deficit, prioritize carbs pre/post lift. Keep oily fish 2x/week or EPA/DHA supplement.
- Week 12: Maintenance calories to consolidate training gains and set up next block (especially if transitioning to any overhead work with physio).

Grocery list staples
- Proteins: chicken, turkey, lean beef, salmon/tuna, eggs, Greek yogurt/skyr, cottage cheese, tofu/tempeh, whey/plant protein.
- Carbs: rice, oats, potatoes, pasta, whole-grain bread, tortillas, fruit, frozen berries, low-fat dairy, rice cakes, cereal.
- Fats: olive oil, avocado, nuts (almonds/walnuts), seeds (chia/flax), nut butters.
- Veg: mixed salad leaves, tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, carrots, broccoli, spinach, crucifers, onions/garlic.
- Flavor: herbs/spices, salsa, mustard, low-sugar sauces.

Special considerations for climbers
- Keep finger/forearm tissues hydrated and fueled: include carbs in the hour pre-session.
- Avoid aggressive deficits before long climbing days; use training-day calories on climbing days too.
- Sodium: if sessions cause heavy sweating or you train in heat, add salt to meals and consider an electrolyte tab in 500–750 mL water.

This plan is flexible and portion-based. Set exact grams using her current bodyweight and adjust every 2–3 weeks from real-world progress while protecting recovery and shoulder health.

Below is a 12-week, 2x/week cardio plan layered onto the existing program to rebuild aerobic capacity for long climbing days without aggravating the shoulder. It emphasizes low-impact, mostly lower-body-dominant modalities, steady aerobic base, and later mixed aerobic power. Keep all shoulder positions below shoulder height; no hanging or overhead arm swing. Integrate with strength days so fatigue doesn’t interfere with scapular control work.

General rules
- Intensity anchor: Use RPE or heart rate. Aim mostly Zone 2 (RPE 4–6/10; conversational; ~60–70% HRmax) with small doses of Zone 3–4 later.
- Pain-free only: No shoulder pain during or after. Keep hands neutral/low on any implements.
- Breathing: Nasal or calm mouth breathing during Z2 to reinforce easy pacing.
- Progression: Increase time before intensity. If any shoulder symptoms, drop intensity, choose a more supported modality, or switch to walking.
- Modalities (choose shoulder-friendly): incline treadmill/hiking, stair mill, stationary bike, spin bike, elliptical with fixed/low handles, sled pushes, brisk outdoor walks (use light arms), rowing is optional only if fully pain-free and arms remain low with neutral grip; otherwise skip.

Weekly placement
- 2 cardio days/week.
- Preferred: Day after UB-A and after UB-B, or on lower-body days, leaving at least 24 hours before the heaviest upper-body session.
- Avoid back-to-back high-tension forearm days with long cardio gripping; use bike or treadmill those weeks.

Warm-up and cool-down (each session)
- 5–8 min warm-up ramp to target HR (start easy).
- 3–5 min cool-down + calf/hip flexor/hamstring mobility.
- Hydrate: 500–750 mL water; add electrolytes for >45–60 min or in heat.

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Aerobic base and tissue tolerance
- Goal: Build steady-state capacity and leg endurance with minimal shoulder involvement.

Week 1
- Cardio 1: Stationary bike Z2, 30 min continuous, RPE 4–5.
- Cardio 2: Incline treadmill hike Z2, 25–30 min, 5–8% grade, RPE 4–5.

Week 2
- Cardio 1: Bike Z2, 35 min.
- Cardio 2: Incline hike Z2, 30–35 min, maintain gait mechanics; keep hands by sides or lightly on rail below shoulder height.

Week 3
- Cardio 1: Bike Z2, 40 min.
- Cardio 2: Stair mill Z2, 25–30 min, light fingertip support, shoulders relaxed down.

Week 4 (deload with strength deload)
- Cardio 1: Easy Z2 of choice, 25–30 min.
- Cardio 2: Brisk walk outdoors, 30–40 min, varied terrain if available.

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Extend duration; introduce tempo
- Goal: Longer steady pieces and controlled tempo intervals (no sprinting). Maintain shoulder-friendly positions.

Week 5
- Cardio 1: Bike Z2, 45 min.
- Cardio 2: Incline hike Z2, 40 min.

Week 6
- Cardio 1: Z2 continuous 50 min (bike or hike).
- Cardio 2: Tempo intervals on bike: 4 x 4 min at upper Z2/low Z3 (RPE 6–7) with 3 min easy Z1–2 between. Total 40–45 min.

Week 7
- Cardio 1: Long Z2, 55–60 min (hike preferred for specificity; add hills if available).
- Cardio 2: Stair mill: 6 x 3 min at RPE 6–7, 2 min easy between. Total ~40–45 min.

Week 8 (deload with strength deload)
- Cardio 1: Easy Z2 35–40 min.
- Cardio 2: Brisk outdoor walk/hike 40–45 min, relaxed.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Specific endurance and aerobic power
- Goal: Build capacity for sustained efforts and rolling terrain—mimic long approaches and easy climbing mileage. Introduce mixed-terrain sessions and short surges without spiking HR too high.

Week 9
- Cardio 1: Long Z2 hike 60–70 min (outdoor if possible; carry light pack 2–3 kg if shoulder allows; keep straps low and symmetric).
- Cardio 2: Bike tempo set: 3 x 8 min at RPE 6–7, 4 min easy between. Total ~50 min.

Week 10
- Cardio 1: Long Z2 70–80 min (mix flats + hills).
- Cardio 2: Rolling intervals on treadmill: 8 min Z2 + 2 min Z3 repeat x3 (total work 30 min) + warm-up/cool-down = ~45–50 min.

Week 11
- Cardio 1: Specific hike 75–90 min. If outdoors, aim continuous ascent/descent; use poles only if grip is relaxed and shoulders stay down.
- Cardio 2: Bike aerobic power: 6 x 2 min at RPE 7–8 (high Z3/low Z4), 2–3 min easy between. Total 35–40 min plus warm-up/cool-down.

Week 12 (consolidate)
- Cardio 1: Long Z2 60–75 min, keep it comfortable—test nutrition/hydration strategy for long days.
- Cardio 2: Mixed terrain 45–60 min: alternate 6 min Z2 with 2 min Z3 for 4–5 rounds.

Optional “climbing day prep” hikes (Weeks 9–12)
- If time allows, add 1 easy walk 20–30 min on a separate day to loosen up and build extra low-intensity volume.

Shoulder safeguards during cardio
- Keep arms low with gentle swing; avoid vigorous arm drive.
- On bike, maintain neutral spine, light hands, elbows tucked; don’t bear weight through the sore shoulder—use core/legs.
- On treadmill/stairs, lightly touch rails (don’t lean). Keep “collarbones wide, shoulders in pockets.”

Fueling for cardio days
- Pre: 30–60 g carbs + 15–25 g protein 1–2 hours before long Z2 or tempo sessions.
- During: For efforts >60 min, 20–30 g carbs/hour + electrolytes as needed.
- Post: 25–35 g protein + 40–60 g carbs within 1–2 hours.

Progress checks
- By Week 6: Z2 pace/HR should improve (lower HR at same pace).
- By Week 10–12: 70–90 min continuous Z2 should feel sustainable with minimal next-day fatigue.
- If legs are too fatigued for strength sessions, reduce the longer cardio by 10–20% or move it further from heavy lower-body work.

This two-day cardio plan builds the aerobic base and stamina needed for long climbing days, while respecting the no-overhead constraint and protecting the shoulder throughout the 12-week block.

Below is a progressive hangboard and climbing-specific prep block layered onto the existing 12-week plan while respecting “pain-free range only” and “no overhead loading.” We’ll introduce finger/forearm conditioning and movement prep in Phases 2–3, using shoulder-safe positions (arms below or at shoulder height, elbows slightly bent, scapulae depressed) and supported setups. The aim is to rebuild tissue tolerance for long climbing days without stressing the right subacromial space.

Safety rules (apply to all sessions)
- Absolutely pain-free at the right shoulder; stop immediately if any shoulder pinch, ache, or night pain occurs.
- No passive dead-hangs or overhead lock-offs. We’ll use supported positions: partial weight, elbows 10–30° flexed, scapulae “long and down.”
- Progress fingers before duration/intensity; maintain forearm circulation between sets.
- Warm hands well; keep total hangboard density modest initially to avoid tendon flare.
- Schedule hangboard 1–2x/week, never the day before the heaviest upper-body session. If in doubt, place it on the same day as a lighter UB session, after lifting, or on a separate easy day.

Equipment and setup
- Hangboard mounted at normal height but perform hangs from a raised box/bench so elbows remain below shoulder height with slight bend; or use a portable board at chest height.
- Use pulley/assistance (bands) or a foot-on box to offload bodyweight.
- Grips: prioritize open-hand/half-crimp; avoid full crimp early. Pinches/slopers only if they do not elevate the arm above shoulder height.
- Edge sizes: start with comfortable large jug/20–25 mm edge; progress to 15–20 mm if symptom-free.

Warm-up for all climbing-prep sessions (10–12 min)
- 3–5 min light cardio + forearm blood flow (wrist circles, finger flicks).
- Scapular activation: band serratus punches x12, scapular depressions from a high-incline support x8–10.
- Elbow/forearm: wrist flexion/extension with light DB x12 each, pronation/supination x12, extensor band opens x20.
- Specific: 2–3 submax “touches” on larger jugs/edges with heavy assistance (5–10s each), zero pain.

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Introduce supported hangs and isometrics
Goal: Build finger tendon tolerance, forearm endurance, and scapular control below shoulder height.

Frequency: 1–2 sessions/week (e.g., after UB-C or on a separate easy day). Keep total work 15–20 minutes.

Week 5
- Session A (supported hangs, open-hand)
  - Assisted jug “hangs” with feet on box: 6 x 10s holds, 50–70% BW supported, elbows 10–20° flexed, scapulae depressed. Rest 50–60s.
  - 20–25 mm edge supported holds: 4 x 7s holds, 60–80% BW supported. Rest 60–75s.
  - Forearm flush: easy forearm pump drill 2 x 60s (squeeze soft foam + relax).
- Session B (if tolerable)
  - Repeat Session A with slightly less assistance only if zero next-day symptoms.

Week 6
- Progress by either +2s per hold (up to 12s) or -5–10% assistance. Keep elbows bent and shoulder quiet.
- Add recruitment pulls (assisted): 3 x 3–4 submaximal “grip engagements” of 2–3s on 20–25 mm with heavy assistance; no full BW.

Week 7
- Mixed edges
  - Jugs: 4 x 12s, light assistance.
  - 20–22 mm: 5 x 10s at 30–50% BW offload.
  - 18–20 mm (only if zero symptoms): 3 x 7s with more assistance. Rest 60–90s.
- Add scapular depression isometric at a high-incline support (not overhead): 3 x 10s x 5 reps, relaxed neck.

Week 8 (deload)
- Reduce total sets by ~40–50%. Stay on jugs/20–25 mm only, short holds (8–10s), generous assistance.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Build finger endurance and introduce foot-on board circuits
Goal: Improve local forearm capacity for long climbing days, maintain pain-free shoulder mechanics, and rehearse movement patterns on the wall below/at shoulder height.

Frequency: 2 sessions/week preferred, 20–30 minutes each.

Week 9
- Hangboard Session
  - Repeaters (assisted, open-hand) on 20–22 mm: 6 x (7s on, 3s off) per set, 2 sets, 2–3 min between sets. Aim 30–50% BW offload. Elbows 10–20° flexed.
  - Jugs: 2 x 20s easy flush holds with very light load.
- Foot-on Board Circuit (Technique Endurance)
  - Set board at easy angle. Hands stay at or below shoulder height.
  - 4 rounds x 2 min continuous easy movement with feet on, changing hands every 4–6 seconds; 2 min rest. Focus: quiet shoulders, scapulae down, smooth breathing.

Week 10
- Hangboard
  - Repeaters on 18–20 mm (if pain-free last week): 3 sets of 6 reps x (7s on/3s off), 2–3 min between. If too hard, return to 20–22 mm or increase assistance.
  - Optional half-crimp intro: 2 x 6s holds on 20–22 mm with heavy assistance; STRICTLY pain-free.
- Foot-on Circuit
  - 3 x 3 min easy movement, 2 min rest. Incorporate low, easy cross-throughs that do not raise the elbow above shoulder height.

Week 11
- Hangboard
  - Density hangs (assisted): 4 x 20s at 20–22 mm + 4 x 10s at 18–20 mm. Rest 60–90s.
  - Recruitment pulls: 3 x 3 submax engagements on best edge with more assistance than you think you need.
- Movement Endurance
  - ARC-style easy mileage below shoulder height: 2 x 8–10 min continuous traversing/low-angle climbing with feet always on and no dynamic moves; 3–4 min rest between. Maintain RPE 5–6, forearm pump manageable.

Week 12 (consolidate/test)
- Hangboard
  - Choose the most joint-friendly protocol:
    - Option A: Repeaters 3 x 6 (7s/3s) on 18–20 mm with steady assistance.
    - Option B: Density 5 x 20s on 20–22 mm with slightly less assistance than Week 11.
  - Note perceived exertion, skin, and any shoulder sensations to guide next block.
- Movement Endurance
  - ARC 1 x 12–15 min continuous easy climbing/traversing, still below shoulder height, smooth breathing. If any shoulder hint, stop and shake out.

Session placement and weekly flow
- Good pairings:
  - Day 1: UB-A + optional short hangboard (post-lift) if shoulder feels great.
  - Day 3: Cardio long Z2.
  - Day 4: UB-B.
  - Day 5: Hangboard + Foot-on Board Circuit (standalone).
  - Day 6: UB-C + easy cardio or outdoor walk.
  - Adjust to keep at least 24–36 hours between the most finger-heavy day and any high-grip accessory work.
- If forearm or shoulder tissues feel tender, skip the second hangboard that week.

Climbing wall integration guidelines (all Phases)
- Phases 1–2: Limit to very easy circuits/traverses with hands at/below shoulder height, feet always on, RPE 3–5, 15–25 minutes total once or twice per week.
- Phase 3: Expand to 30–40 minutes total per week of easy mileage, broken into 2–3 bouts. No dynos, gastons, lock-offs above shoulder height, or hard underclings.

Recovery and monitoring for climbing prep
- Skin care: file calluses lightly; moisturize at night; wash chalk off post-session.
- Tendon care: stop 2–3 reps shy of form breakdown; easy forearm flush (light squeezing + wrist circles) between sets; contrast temperature is optional.
- Soreness rules: forearm muscle fatigue is fine; A2 pulley pain, sharp joint pain, or shoulder ache is not. If symptoms >24 hours, cut next week’s hangboard volume by 30–50% and increase assistance/edge size.
- Nutrition tie-in: include 20–30 g fast protein + 30–60 g carbs within 1 hour of hangboard/ARC sessions. Hydrate well; add sodium on longer days.

Next-block progression (after Week 12, with physio clearance)
- Gradually raise arm angle and reintroduce gentle overhead positions:
  - Dowel/scapular elevation control drills pain-free.
  - Assisted partial dead-hangs with elbows slightly bent, very short durations.
  - Introduce small ranges of overhead lock-off isometrics on jugs with heavy assistance.
  - Start easy vertical pulling (assisted) and high-step reaches only when cleared.

This add-on gives you a shoulder-safe, progressive path to rebuild finger strength and forearm endurance while reinforcing scapular control, setting her up for longer, pain-free climbing days.

- Keep pressing/pulling strength high but streamlined.

- Consolidate cardio into one long Z2 and one aerobic-power session weekly to support long days.

Guiding rules for the peak
- Pain-free range only and no overhead loading still apply. If any shoulder symptoms arise, immediately revert to prior angles/loads and reduce volume.
- Prioritize quality sleep, carbs around key sessions, and reduce non-essential fatigue.

Phase 3 revised overview
- Weekly structure (ideal):

Weeks 9–11: Intensification

Week 9
- UB-A
  - A1 DB bench (neutral): 5x5, RPE 7–8
  - A2 Rear delt fly: 3x12–15, easy
  - B1 Landmine press: 4x6/side, RPE 7–8, stop at shoulder height

Week 10 (micro-deload early week, then hit a higher-quality hangboard)
- UB-A
  - DB bench: 4x4–5, RPE 7
  - Landmine press: 3x5/side, RPE 7
  - Cuff/scap: maintain 2–3 easy sets each
- UB-B
  - Chest-supported row: 4x4–5, RPE 7

- Hangboard (key session this week—separate day, fresh)

- Movement Endurance
  - ARC/traverse: 2 x 8–10 min continuous easy climbing below shoulder height, 3–4 min rest.

Week 11 (peak training load on fingers and specific endurance)
- UB-A

  - Landmine press: 4x4–5/side, RPE 7–8
  - Minimal accessories: 1–2 light sets rear delts + cuff

  - Chest-supported row: 5x4, RPE 8
  - 1-arm cable row: 3x6–8/side with 2s peak hold
  - Light face pulls 2x12–15
- Hangboard (key intensity)

  - Option B (if repeaters were marginal): Density 5 x 20s on 20–22 mm with modest assistance, 60–90s rest.
  - Finish with 2 x 10s recruitment touches on best edge, heavy assistance.
- Movement Endurance (specific)
  - ARC 1 x 12–15 min continuous traverse/very easy mileage, below shoulder height. Aim even breathing, slight forearm pump that stays manageable.
- Cardio
  - Long Z2 75–90 min hike (practice fueling and footwear).

Week 12: Taper and peak for the trip
Goal: Keep intensity touches, drop volume 40–60%, freshen up skin/forearms, and arrive feeling springy. Climbing-specific work shifts to rehearsal and confidence.

- Early-week UB-A (Mon/Tue if leaving late week)
  - DB bench: Work up to 1–2 top sets of 3–4 at RPE ~7, then stop.
  - Landmine press: 2–3x4/side at RPE 6–7.
  - Cuff/scap: 2 light sets each.
- Early-week Hangboard (48–72h before travel/day 1 climb)
  - Recruitment focus only (no fatigue): 3 rounds of 3 x 3s submax engagements on 18–22 mm with generous assistance; 45–60s between reps, 2–3 min between rounds.
  - Optional 2 x 10s density holds on 20–22 mm at very easy effort.
- Mid-week UB-B
  - Chest-supported row: 3x3–4 at RPE 7; 1–2 light accessory sets. Out the door in 30–40 min.
- Movement prep (one short session, 24–48h before first climbing day)
  - Easy traverse 10–12 min continuous or 2 x 6 min, hands ≤ shoulder height, smooth breathing, zero pump.
- Cardio this week
  - One 45–60 min Z2 easy hike or spin early in the week to keep the engine; skip the aerobic power session.
- Mobility/recovery
  - Daily 5–8 min: T-spine mobility, gentle pec minor stretch (arm below shoulder), scapular activation.
  - Sleep 8+ hours; hydrate; keep carbs higher 24–48h pre-trip.

Fueling adjustments for the peak
- Weeks 9–11: Keep recomposition target but don’t underfuel key sessions. Ensure 60–90 g carbs pre key hangboard/ARC and 40–80 g post with 25–35 g protein.
- Week 12: Move to maintenance calories (+200–300 kcal/day), prioritize carbs. Day before travel: 5–7 g/kg carbs, normal protein, moderate salt/water.

Readiness and monitoring
- Green lights: No shoulder pain during/after sessions, steady improvement in repeaters quality, lower HR at same Z2 pace, and ability to sustain 12–15 min continuous easy climbing with manageable pump.
- Red flags: Night shoulder pain, pinching with landmine/press, finger A2 tenderness. If present, reduce hangboard by 50%, swap edges up in size, increase assistance, and keep only recruitment touches.

Trip-week warm-up template (on climbing days)
- 8–10 min brisk walk + forearm blood flow
- Shoulder: band serratus punches x10, scap depressions x8, gentle active ER x10
- 2–3 assisted recruitment touches on good edges (3s each)
- Progress into easy jugs and easy problems/routes to shoulder height before increasing difficulty or duration

This intensification and taper keep intensity where it matters—rows, DB bench/landmine, aerobic power, and especially finger/forearm endurance—while trimming fatigue so she arrives in Week 12 fresh and confident for long climbing days, all within shoulder-safe constraints.

Here’s a shoulder-safe mobility and prep plan to layer onto the 12-week program. It prioritizes thoracic mobility, scapular mechanics, pain-free glenohumeral ROM, forearm/elbow tissue care, and hips/ankles for better footwork. No end-range shoulder elevation or painful impingement arcs. Use pain-free range only.

How to use
- Frequency: 10–15 minutes most days (5–6x/week). Keep it shortest on heavy days; longer on off days.
- Order: Do “Prep (pre-lift/climb)” before upper-body and hangboard sessions. Do “Recovery (post-session/evening)” on training and rest days.
- Effort: Movements should feel relieving, not strenuous. Stop if you feel sharp pain, joint pinch, or next-day ache in the right shoulder.

Daily prep block (6–10 minutes)
1) Breathing and ribcage stack (90/90 with feet on wall)
- 3–4 breaths x 3 sets. Inhale nose, exhale fully through mouth, ribs down, light abs. Promotes scapular position (posterior tilt) without cranking the shoulder.

2) Thoracic spine opener (side-lying “open book”)
- 6–8 reps/side, slow, keep shoulder below/at shoulder height. Focus on rotating through ribs, not cranking the arm back.

3) Serratus activation
- Band serratus punches (elbow close, arm ≤ shoulder height): 2x10/side, reach without shrugging.
- Option alt days: Wall serratus slide (stop at shoulder height) with mini-band around forearms: 2x8–10.

4) Scapular control
- High-incline or bar-supported scapular depression/retraction: 2x8 easy pulses, “long neck, shoulders in pockets,” no elevation.

5) Shoulder rotational priming (pain-free)
- Cable or band external rotation at 0–30° abduction (towel under elbow): 2x10 slow. Keep ribs down, no pinch.

Post-session/evening recovery block (8–12 minutes)
1) T-spine mobility (child’s pose side reach)
- 2x20–30s/side, breathe into the side ribs.

2) Pec minor/anterolateral chest (low-angle doorway)
- 2x20–30s/side with arm below shoulder height. Do not let shoulder roll forward.

3) Posterior cuff tissue and rotation
- Sleeper stretch (gentle): 2x20s/side in pain-free range. Neck long, scapula gently set; stop if any pinch.
- Follow with 1x12 light band ER for blood flow.

4) Scapular upward/downward rotation balance
- Prone low Y to ~100–120° (not overhead) on incline bench: 2x10, slow 2–3s lowers.

5) Forearm and elbow care
- Wrist flexor/extensor glides: 8–10 slow reps each direction/side.
- Extensor band “open/close”: 1–2 sets x 20.
- Gentle radial/ulnar nerve sliders (only if symptom-free): 5–8 slow reps/side, no tingling provocation.

Weekly mobility emphasis (phase-specific)
Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Calm symptoms, restore scap control and T-spine motion
- Add 2–3x/week:
  - Quadruped rocking with active shoulder packing: 2x8–10, small painless range.
  - Seated thoracic extension over foam roller (mid-back only): 2x6 slow extensions; keep neck neutral.
  - Gentle isometric ER/IR at neutral (towel under elbow): 2x5 x 5s each direction.

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progress ROM, add controlled end-range below shoulder height
- Add 2x/week:
  - Side-lying flexion arcs: draw small arcs to just below shoulder height, 2x8–10, focus on humeral head centered.
  - Scapular posterior tilt drill on wall: forearms on wall, 90° elbow bend; practice “tip shoulder blades back and down” without shrug, 2x8 holds x 5s.
  - Thoracic rotation with reach: half-kneel, hand on dowel at chest height, rotate from ribs, 2x6/side.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Maintain mobility, sharpen specificity, protect during peak
- Keep daily prep brief and crisp; avoid aggressive stretching that leaves tissues lax before key sessions.
- Add on non-lifting days:
  - Band-assisted lat/upper back stretch at low angle (hand below shoulder): 2x20–30s/side.
  - Scapular CARs (controlled articular rotations) in low abduction: 2 slow circles each direction/side, no pinch.
- Pre-trip week (Week 12):
  - Emphasize breathing, serratus activation, and T-spine openers; cut long static stretches. Aim to feel “springy.”

Lower-body/hip-ankle mobility for climbing footwork (2–3x/week, 6–8 minutes)
- Ankle dorsiflexion rocks (knee-to-wall): 2x10/side, light end-range pulses.
- Calf soft-tissue (optional): 30–45s each side with ball/roller, then 1x10 ankle pumps.
- 90/90 hip switches: 2x6–8 slow reps, upright torso.
- Adductor rock-backs (knees wide): 2x10 slow reps; keep spine neutral.
- Hip flexor half-kneel stretch with posterior tilt: 2x20–30s/side; add reaching opposite arm to chest height only.

Micro-mobility “snacks” (2–3 minutes, anytime)
- 3 deep breaths (90/90 or tall-kneel).
- 10 scap depressions at a counter.
- 10 wrist circles + 10 extensor band opens.
- 6 open books/side.

Red flags and modifications
- Any subacromial pinch, night pain, or tingling: stop that drill; replace with breathing, T-spine work, and light band ER only until calm.
- If sleeper stretch provokes symptoms, swap for cross-body posterior cuff stretch at low angle: 2x20s/side, scapula set, gentle.

Progress checks
- By Week 4: Easier scap “set,” less neck tension; band ER feels smoother.
- By Week 8: Greater pain-free flexion to shoulder height with cleaner scap posterior tilt.
- By Week 12: Prep feels quick and effective; no post-session shoulder ache; improved comfort during long, easy traverses.

This mobility plan supports pain-free mechanics, complements the strength/hangboard work, and helps her arrive at Week 12 feeling open, stable, and ready for long climbing days—without violating the no-overhead constraint.

Here’s a Saturday “finisher day” you can plug in across the 12 weeks. It’s full-body, short, and fun, with zero overhead loading and shoulder-safe options. Keep it 25–35 minutes, RPE 6–8, and stop if the right shoulder complains. Use a timer, play music, and keep transitions snappy.

General rules
- Pain-free only; no overhead pressing, vertical pulling, or high abduction.
- Favor neutral grips; elbows close to the body; scapulae “long and down.”
- Choose 1 circuit from the week’s menu; rotate for variety.
- Warm-up: 5–7 min (bike or brisk walk) + 1 round of: band serratus punches x10, light KB deadlift x10, incline scap push-ups x8, bodyweight split squat x8/leg.

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Groove, low impact, technique focus
Pick 1 circuit

Option A: EMOM 20 (every minute on the minute x 20; 5 rounds of each station)
- Min 1: Chest-supported DB row x 8–10 (neutral grip)
- Min 2: Landmine press to shoulder height x 6–8/side (half-kneel)
- Min 3: Goblet squat x 10–12
- Min 4: Bike calories (easy-moderate) or 45s Z2 spin
Scale loads to finish with 10–15s spare each minute. If any shoulder hint on landmine, use incline push-up x 6–10 instead.

Option B: 4-station continuous circuit x 4 rounds (work 40s, rest 20s)
- A1: Incline push-up (height to pain-free)
- A2: Sled push (light-moderate, 20–25 m) or farmers carry 30–40 m
- A3: Chest-supported rear delt fly (thumbs up)
- A4: Alternating reverse lunge (bodyweight or light DBs)
2 min easy spin walk between Rounds 2 and 3 if needed.

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Add intensity and unilateral work
Pick 1 circuit

Option C: “Carry and Engine” AMRAP 25
- A1: Farmer carry 30–40 m heavy-ish, neutral grip
- A2: 1-arm landmine press x 8/side (standing or half-kneel, to shoulder height)
- A3: 1-arm cable row x 10/side (to navel, 2s squeeze)
- A4: DB RDL x 10
- A5: Bike erg x 12–15 cals (or 60s Z2–Z3)
Move smoothly; keep shoulder quiet. Swap A2 for incline push-ups if needed.

Option D: Ascending ladder 12 minutes + Finisher 6 minutes
- Ladder (12 min AMRAP, add 1 rep each round): DB floor press (neutral) + goblet squat, start at 3/3, 4/4, 5/5, etc., staying pain-free ROM.
- Finisher: 6 min alternating every 30s: chest-supported row x 8–10 and brisk walk on incline.
Cool down 3–5 min.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Peak-friendly, spicy but short; keep shoulders fresh
Pick 1 circuit

Option E: Power-endurance mash-up (20–24 min)
- Block 1: 6 min on a clock
  - 30s sled push (moderate) + 30s incline push-up (submax)
- Block 2: 6 min
  - 30s chest-supported row (hard 8–10) + 30s bike (moderate-hard)
- Block 3: 6–8 min
  - 20s landmine press/side (controlled to shoulder height) + 20s farmer hold (heavy, neutral) + 20s brisk walk
Rest 60–90s between blocks.

Option F: “Grip ‘n’ Grit” EMOM 24 (4 rounds)
- Min 1: Chest-supported row x 8 heavy
- Min 2: DB floor press (neutral) x 8–10
- Min 3: Trap-bar deadlift x 5–6 (or DB RDL x 10 if no trap bar)
- Min 4: Carry of choice 30–40 m (farmer or bottoms-up light)
Keep reps crisp; stop 2 shy of failure.

Week 12 (trip taper) Saturday tweak
- Keep it light and snappy: choose Option E Block 1 only + 10 min easy spin, or a 20-minute easy Z2 hike with 3 short sled pushes. No grinders, no skin or finger fatigue.

Optional “fun extras” to sprinkle in, shoulder-safe
- Med-ball chest pass to wall (below shoulder height) 6x5
- Light battle ropes with elbows tucked 4x20s on/40s off
- Box step-ups (low) with light DBs
- Low TRX row (keep elbows close, adjustable body angle)
- Core finishers: dead bug x 10/side, suitcase carry 20–30 m/side, Pallof press holds 20–30s/side

Monitoring and swaps
- If landmine press provokes symptoms: swap for incline push-up, cable press at chest height, or DB floor press.
- If gripping feels overcooked (from hangboard), lighten carries or use sled pushes instead.
- Keep total elbow-to-hand volume in check the same week as key hangboard sessions; choose circuits heavier on legs/sled.

This Saturday finisher gives her a satisfying, full-body hit that complements the program, keeps intensity fun, and stays within no-overhead and pain-free constraints—plus it’s easy to taper in Week 12 before the trip.

Here’s the complete 12-week program summary for your 29-year-old recreational climber with right subacromial impingement. Constraints: pain-free range only; no overhead loading. Full gym available. Program includes upper-body strength (primary), cardio 2x/week, hangboard/climbing prep (later phases), mobility, nutrition, and a Saturday finisher. Structure is week-by-week with phased progression, deloads, and a Week-12 peak for a climbing trip.

Global guardrails
- Absolutely pain-free; stop any exercise that causes shoulder pain or next-day ache. Prioritize neutral/semisupinated grips, elbows 30–45° from torso on presses, and scapulae “long and down.” Avoid overhead presses/pulls, vertical hangs, high abduction, kips, dynamic reaches, or gastons.
- Progression order: range of motion (pain-free) → load → sets/reps. RPE 6–7 early, up to 7–8 by mid/late phases if symptom-free.
- Weekly cadence (ideal): 3 UB sessions (A/B/C), 2 cardio, 1–2 hangboard/climbing-prep (Phases 2–3), daily brief mobility, Saturday finisher (optional and scaled).

Warm-up (all sessions, 10–12 min)
- 3–5 min light cardio
- T-spine: open books 6–8/side
- Scap activation: band serratus punches x12; scap depressions x8–10 at incline/support
- Cuff: band/cable ER at 0–30° abd x10/side
- 2–3 progressive warm-up sets for first two lifts

PHASE 1 (Weeks 1–4): Control and tolerance
Goal: Pain-free movement, scapular mechanics, cuff/mid-back endurance, grip tolerance. 2–3 UB sessions/week.

UB-A (horizontal push + cuff/scap)
- DB floor press (neutral), pain-free ROM
- Chest-supported rear delt fly (thumbs up)
- Landmine press to shoulder height (half-kneel)
- Cable ER at 0–30° abd
- Serratus wall slides (to shoulder height), Prone low Y (100–120°)

UB-B (horizontal pull)
- Chest-supported row (neutral)
- Serratus reach/downward punch (cable)
- 1-arm cable row (low to navel)
- Iso retraction/depression holds (supported)
- Hammer curl, rope pressdown

UB-C (optional light technique)
- Incline push-up (height to pain-free)
- Wrist pronation/supination
- Farmer carry (neutral grip), light-moderate
- Scap pull-up isometrics at bottom (depression only)

Loading guide Weeks 1–3: 3–4 sets x 8–12 reps main work at RPE 6–7; controlled tempo (e.g., 3-1-1/3-1-2). Progress small ROM/load each week if pain-free. Week 4 deload: −30–40% volume, same/light load, technique focus.

PHASE 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength and unilateral control
Goal: Increase horizontal press/pull strength; refine scap/cuff; introduce isometric mid-range work. Prefer 3 UB sessions/week.

UB-A (press emphasis)
- DB bench (neutral) 4x6–8 (progress to 5x5 by W7)
- Rear delt fly (pause)
- Landmine press 4x6 (to shoulder height)
- Cable ER at 45° abd
- Serratus wall slides; Pallof press

UB-B (pull emphasis)
- 1-arm chest-supported row 4x8/side
- Face pull to chest/neck height (light, elbows low)
- Seated cable row 4x8–10 (neutral)
- Prone T/Y holds (below overhead)
- Reverse or hammer curls; triceps cable ext (neutral)

UB-C (unilateral + grip)
- Incline push-up (lower incline across phase; flat only if fully pain-free)
- Landmine press isometrics (safe angle)
- Carries: farmer or bottoms-up (light)
- Scap depressions

Week 8 deload: −40% sets, RPE 6–7, ROM quality and scap/cuff drills.

PHASE 3 (Weeks 9–12): Intensification, endurance, peak
Goal: Solidify strength, build climbing-specific finger/forearm endurance and aerobic power, and taper for a Week-12 trip (no overhead loading).

UB-A (press emphasis; keep crisp)
- DB bench: 5x5 (W9), 4x4–5 (W10 deload), 4x3–4 (W11), W12 1–2 top sets 3–4 at RPE ~7
- Landmine press: 4x6 → 3–4x4–5; stop at shoulder height
- Rear delts + cuff: 2–3 light sets

UB-B (heavy pull emphasis)
- Chest-supported row: 5x5 (W9), 4x4–5 (W10 deload), 5x4 (W11), W12 3x3–4 at RPE 7
- 1-arm cable row with 2s peak holds: 3x6–10/side
- Face pulls light; T/Y holds light

UB-C (keep or drop depending on fatigue)
- Alternating DB floor press, unilateral rows, carries, core; stop 2 reps shy of failure

CARDIO 2x/week (all phases; shoulder-safe modalities: bike, incline treadmill/hike, stair mill, sled pushes, brisk walk)
- Phase 1: Build to 40–45 min Z2
- Phase 2: Extend to 50–60 min Z2 + introduce tempo (e.g., 4x4 min RPE 6–7)
- Phase 3: One long Z2 70–90 min hike + one aerobic-power session (e.g., bike 6x2–3 min RPE 7–8). Week 12: 45–60 min easy Z2 only

HANGBOARD + CLIMBING-SPECIFIC PREP (Phase 2–3; 1–2x/week)
Rules: Pain-free shoulder; elbows 10–30° flexed; scapulae depressed; supported hangs with assistance; open-hand/half-crimp; no overhead dead-hangs/lock-offs.

Phase 2 (W5–8)
- Supported holds on jugs/20–25 mm: 6–12s holds, 4–6 sets, 30–70% BW offload
- Add gentle recruitment pulls (assisted) and 18–20 mm only if symptom-free
- Week 8 deload: reduce to easy assisted jugs/20–25 mm

Phase 3 (W9–12) with Peak
- W9: Repeaters 2–3 sets on 20–22 mm (6 x 7s on/3s off), plus foot-on board circuits 3 x 3 min
- W10: Key session—repeaters on 18–20 mm (3 x 6) if pain-free; ARC 2 x 8–10 min low-angle traversing below shoulder height
- W11: Peak finger load—repeaters 4 x 6 on 18–20 mm or density 5 x 20s on 20–22 mm; ARC 12–15 min continuous easy traverse
- W12 Taper: Recruitment touches only (3 rounds: 3 x 3s, heavy assistance) + short easy traverse 10–12 min; avoid fatigue

SATURDAY FINISHER (25–35 min, fun, full-body; rotate options; no overhead)
- Phase 1 picks: EMOM 20 (rows, landmine to shoulder height or incline push-ups, goblet squats, easy bike) or 4-station circuit x4 (incline push-up, sled/carry, rear delts, reverse lunge)
- Phase 2 picks: AMRAP 25 (farmer carry, 1-arm landmine press, 1-arm cable row, DB RDL, bike) or 12-min ladder (DB floor press + goblet squat) + 6-min finisher (rows/walk)
- Phase 3 picks: 20–24 min blocks (sled + incline push-ups; rows + bike; landmine + farmer hold + brisk walk) or EMOM 24 (row, DB floor press, trap-bar/DB RDL, carry)
- Week 12: keep light and short (10–20 min easy work; no finger fatigue)

MOBILITY (6–15 min most days; pain-free only)
Prep (pre-session, 6–10 min)
- 90/90 breathing (3–4 breaths x 3)
- Open books 6–8/side
- Band serratus punches 2x10; wall slide to shoulder height 2x8–10
- Scap depressions 2x8
- Band/cable ER at 0–30° abd 2x10

Recovery (post/evening, 8–12 min)
- Child’s pose side reach 2x20–30s/side
- Low-angle pec doorway stretch 2x20–30s/side
- Sleeper stretch gentle 2x20s/side (swap to cross-body if provocative) + light band ER 1x12
- Prone low Y 2x10
- Forearm care: wrist flex/ext glides 8–10 reps; extensor band opens 1–2x20

Lower-body mobility (2–3x/week, 6–8 min)
- Ankle dorsiflexion rocks 2x10/side; 90/90 hip switches 2x6–8; adductor rock-backs 2x10; half-kneel hip flexor stretch 2x20–30s/side

NUTRITION (recomposition focus, supports recovery)
- Calories: Train days ~14–15 kcal/lb (30–33 kcal/kg); Rest days ~12–13 kcal/lb (26–29 kcal/kg). Adjust to lose ~0.25–0.5% BW/week; go to maintenance in Week 12.
- Protein: 0.8–1.0 g/lb (1.8–2.2 g/kg) in 3–5 feedings of 25–40 g.
- Carbs: 1.5–2.0 g/lb (3.3–4.4 g/kg) train days; 1.0–1.5 g/lb (2.2–3.3 g/kg) rest days; time most pre/post training.
- Fat: 0.3–0.4 g/lb (0.7–0.9 g/kg).
- Micronutrients: oily fish 2x/week or 1–2 g EPA/DHA; vitamin D3 1,000–2,000 IU if low sun; magnesium 200–400 mg if sleep/cramps; optional collagen 10–15 g + ~50 mg vitamin C 30–60 min pre-training.
- Peri-workout: 25–40 g protein + 60–90 g carbs 60–120 min pre; 25–40 g protein + 40–80 g carbs post. Long cardio/hangs >60–90 min: 20–40 g carbs/hr + electrolytes.
- Week 12: raise to maintenance (+200–300 kcal/day), carbs higher; day before trip 5–7 g/kg carbs.

CARDIO placement
- Place the long Z2 the day after UB-A or UB-B; place the aerobic-power session 48 h away from the longest hangboard/ARC. Avoid back-to-back high-grip days.

PROGRESSION AND DELoadS
- W4 and W8: deload volume 30–40% (technique/ROM focus).
- W9–11: intensify strength (lower reps, RPE 7–8), hangboard repeaters progress (if pain-free), and specific endurance (ARC).
- W12: taper volume 40–60%, keep light intensity touches; arrive fresh.

READINESS/RED FLAGS
- Green: zero shoulder pain during/after, improved ROM, lower HR at same Z2 pace, higher quality repeaters/rows/presses.
- Red: shoulder pinch or night pain; finger A2 tenderness; nerve symptoms. Respond by reducing volume 30–50%, increasing assistance/edge size, swapping to more supported variants, and consulting physio as needed.

Example weekly layout (Phase 3 intensification)
- Mon: UB-A + short recruitment hangboard
- Tue: Long Z2 hike
- Wed: UB-B
- Thu: Hangboard (repeaters) + foot-on or ARC
- Fri: Rest or mobility walk
- Sat: Finisher (shorter if forearms cooked)
- Sun: Aerobic power bike (or swap with Tue if preferred)

This summary links all components—strength, cardio, hangboard/technique, mobility, nutrition, finisher day—into a cohesive, shoulder-safe 12-week plan that peaks her for a Week-12 climbing trip without overhead loading. Adjust loads/angles weekly based on symptom-free progress and performance.
